paragraphs: Apple is testing adding two more widgets to the iPhone Duo’s Lock Screen. The “complication column,” which lets Duo users choose from various widgets, is switched off for now, though.
The experiment shows that Apple is still exploring ways to maximize use of screen space on the first-ever foldable iPhone. But it remains unclear if or when the customization tweak will go live.

The first foldable iPhone, which hit stores a month ago, forced Apple to rethink the iOS user interface from the ground up. The result is a short Home Screen on the outer display, with familiar icons moved to the right, and a delightful animation as you unfold the device to reveal its wide inner screen. New multitasking and StandBy modes take advantage of the new form factor.

For nearly two decades, the iPhone’s basic interface has revolved around a rectangular screen and a grid of apps. A foldable demands a different approach — and Apple continues to tweak the user experience.

Currently, widgets on the iPhone Duo‘s Lock Screen sit along the right edge of the screen, at the top and bottom. Two default shortcuts, Camera and Flashlight, sit at the bottom-right corner of the screen, while the combined Wi-Fi and cellular icon appears at the top right

Code explorer pdfu spotted a change to this setup that has not yet been implemented and wrote about it Sunday on X. The “complication column” adds a spot for two additional widgets along the right edge of the screen, between the current widgets.

An accompanying screen recording posted by pdfu shows how it would work. Tapping and holding the iPhone Duo’s Home Screen would bring up a customization option. Then users could pick from widgets to add, including Batteries, Calendar, Clock and Fitness.
Apple has tested a “complication column” for iPhone Duo’s Lock Screen. It fits two circular widgets along the right edge.
